label: Start of copy phase (<DEL> step and first echoed token), sequences beginning with c/h/2/f/u
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.03% of steps). Its position is clear: 64% of activation mass falls at recall_idx==1, the first copy-phase step, where the input is the echoed first original token. Another 18% falls on the <DEL> step. It almost never fires during the original phase (6% of mass) or late in the copy phase. It is strongly selective for the first original token: c (11x lift, 36% of mass), h (7x), then f, u and 2. Sequences with y or 1 at the second or third position (the next output) also raise the rate (next_out y/1 about 10x). Strongest activations: sequences starting with c followed by y/h/1/c (e.g. c c y y ... <DEL> c). Even inside this context it fires only on a small fraction of sequences (precision ~1%; ~11% when restricted to first_tok c with a y anywhere in the sequence). The rest of its selectivity seems to be a combinatorial dependence on the early original tokens that no simple predicate captures. Location plus first-token predicate: mass recall ~0.76 on dev, but precision is very low.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: in_tok=h (+5.45), in_tok=f (+4.67), phase=2 & in_tok=u (+3.68), orig2=y (+3.02), orig3=y (+2.98), in_tok=c (+2.96). Lower it: phase=2 (-3.86), recall_idx=-1 (-3.60), prev3_tok=- (-3.00), orig3=i (-2.33).
